steps.title: Early 2025: buying ahead
text: Expecting new tariffs, [US](USA) importers rushed to bring goods in. US imports were **25%** higher in January 2025 than a year earlier and **32%** higher in March.
March 2025's **$343 billion** is the highest monthly figure in this data. The map shows the change in imports from each partner.

steps.title: April 2025: “reciprocal” tariffs
text: On **2 April 2025** the [US](USA) announced an additional tariff of at least 10% on imports from all trading partners, with higher rates for some. Tariffs between the US and [China](CHN) escalated until a 12 May statement in Geneva suspended most of the increases for 90 days.
US imports from the Chinese mainland were **42% lower** in May 2025 than a year earlier, and 44% lower in June. The panel compares US trade with China over time.

steps.title: Who supplied instead
text: For 2025 as a whole, [US](USA) imports from the [Chinese mainland](CHN) fell **30%** to $308 billion, just **9.0%** of US imports and fourth behind the [EU](EU), [Mexico](MEX) and [Canada](CAN).
Imports from [Taiwan, China](TWN) rose 73% to $201 billion and from [Vietnam](VNM) 42% to $194 billion. Total US imports still grew 4.6%, to $3.42 trillion.

steps.title: China's exports keep growing
text: The [Chinese mainland](CHN)'s exports still grew **5.5%** in 2025, to $3.78 trillion. Its exports to the [US](USA) fell 20%, but exports to [Vietnam](VNM) (+22%), the [EU](EU) and [Hong Kong SAR, China](HKG) rose.
Recent months are the first estimates and may be revised.
